bottom_line: In patients stabilised after an acute coronary syndrome, rivaroxaban versus placebo had a primary efficacy endpoint rate of 5.6% vs 7.0% (HR 0.79 [0.60–1.05]).
implications: These data support that, across tested doses, rivaroxaban increased clinically significant bleeding versus placebo (eg, HR 2.21 to 5.06 across 5–20 mg total daily dose) while the primary efficacy endpoint was not statistically different overall (HR 0.79 [0.60–1.05], p=0.10). The results do support a reduction in the main secondary composite of death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (87/2331 [3.9%] vs 62/1160 [5.5%]; HR 0.69 [0.50–0.96], p=0.0270), but do not establish definitive efficacy for the primary composite in this phase II trial.

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase II, dose-escalation trial in patients stabilised after acute coronary syndrome.
major_points.quote: In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase II, dose-escalation study, 3491 participants were randomised at 297 sites in 27 countries.

major_points.text: Randomisation was stratified by investigator decision to use aspirin alone vs aspirin plus a thienopyridine.
major_points.quote: 3491 patients stabilised after an acute coronary syndrome were stratiﬁed on the basis of investigator decision to use aspirin only (stratum 1, n=761) or aspirin plus a thienopyridine (stratum 2, n=2730).

major_points.text: Participants were randomised to placebo or rivaroxaban once daily or twice daily (same total daily dose).
major_points.quote: Participants were randomised within each strata and dose tier with a block randomisation method at 1:1:1 to receive either placebo or rivaroxaban (at doses 5–20 mg) given once daily or the same total daily dose given twice daily.

major_points.text: Primary safety endpoint was clinically significant bleeding (TIMI major, TIMI minor, or requiring medical attention).
major_points.quote: The primary safety endpoint was clinically signiﬁcant bleeding (TIMI major, TIMI minor, or requiring medical attention)

major_points.text: Clinically significant bleeding increased with rivaroxaban in a dose-dependent manner versus placebo.
major_points.quote: Clinically signiﬁcant bleeding (TIMI major, TIMI minor, or requiring medical attention) occurred in a dose-dependent manner: compared with placebo HRs were 2·21 (95% CI 1·25–3·91) for 5 mg, 3·35 (2·31–4·87)

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint did not reach statistical significance for rivaroxaban versus placebo in the entire cohort.

subgroups.text: No heterogeneity in clinically significant bleeding when stratified by multiple baseline factors (listed).
subgroups.quote: there was no heterogeneity in the rates of clinically signiﬁcant bleeding in participants stratiﬁed by age, creatinine clearance, weight, previous myocardial infarction, diabetes, smoking, region, index event, PCI

subgroups.text: Primary efficacy endpoint hazard ratios differed between strata (interaction p=0.034).
subgroups.quote: Compared with placebo, rivaroxaban was associated with an HR of 0·53 (95% CI 0·33–0·84) for death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or severe recurrent ischaemia requiring revascularisation in stratum 1 and an HR of 0·99

subgroups.text: Exploratory interactions noted for age and index event for the primary efficacy endpoint.
subgroups.quote: In exploratory analyses, signiﬁcant interactions were noted on the basis of age (p for interaction=0·007) and index event (p for inter- action=0·042).

harms.text: One fatal bleed occurred (intracranial haemorrhage) in rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily group of stratum 1.
harms.quote: One fatal bleed occurred: a participant in the rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily dose group of stratum 1 presented with an intracranial haemorrhage.

harms.text: Most common adverse event in both groups was chest pain.
harms.quote: The most common adverse event in both groups was chest pain (248/2309 [10·7%] vs 118/1153 [10·2%]).

inclusion_criteria.text: Randomisation occurred 1–7 days after hospital admission for an acute coronary syndrome.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Randomisation occurred 1–7 days after hospital admission for an acute coronary syndrome.

inclusion_criteria.text: Required symptoms suggestive of acute coronary syndrome lasting at least 10 min at rest.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Participants were required to have symptoms suggestive of an acute coronary syndrome that lasted at least 10 min at rest

inclusion_criteria.text: Eligible diagnoses included STEMI or non-STEMI/unstable angina with at least one specified risk criterion.
inclusion_criteria.quote: either a diagnosis of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or a diagnosis of non-STEMI or unstable angina with at least one of the following: raised cardiac enzyme markers, 1 mm or more ST-segment deviation, or a TIMI risk score of 3 or more.

analysis_methods.text: Safety analyses included all participants who received at least one dose of study drug; efficacy analyses were by intention to treat.
analysis_methods.quote: Safety analyses included all participants who received at least one dose of study drug; eﬃcacy analyses were by intention to treat.

analysis_methods.text: Baseline characteristics compared using Wilcoxon rank sum test or t test (continuous) and χ² test (categorical).
analysis_methods.quote: Baseline characteristics were compared with the Wilcoxon rank sum test or t test for continuous variables and the χ² test for categorical variables.

analysis_methods.text: Hazard ratios and 95% CIs calculated using Cox proportional hazards regression; log-rank test stratified by stratum was used for comparisons vs pooled placebo.
analysis_methods.quote: Hazard ratios and 95% CIs were calculated on the basis of Cox proportional hazards regression models. The log-rank test, stratiﬁed by stratum 1 and stratum 2, was used to compare each treatment group to the pooled

analysis_methods.text: Sample size of at least 225 patients per dose tier and stratum chosen to estimate bleeding rate for each treatment.
analysis_methods.quote: The sample size of at least 225 patients per dose tier and stratum was chosen to provide an estimate of the bleeding rate for each treatment.

analysis_methods.text: Trial not powered to test ability of rivaroxaban compared with placebo to reduce efficacy endpoints.
analysis_methods.quote: Moreover, the study was not powered to test the ability of rivaroxaban compared with placebo to reduce eﬃcacy endpoints.

criticisms.text: Trial was not powered to obtain a significant effect for efficacy comparison.
criticisms.quote: Although the eﬃcacy of rivaroxaban compared with placebo was also assessed, this trial was not powered to obtain a signiﬁcant eﬀect.

criticisms.text: Many active treatment groups and small numbers in some individual dosing strategies, making some observations unclear.
criticisms.quote: some individual dosing strategies were assessed in only a small number of patients. Consequently, in assessment of individual dosing strategies, whether some observations are due to chance or pathobiology is unclear

criticisms.text: Primary efficacy endpoint results across strata require careful interpretation due to heterogeneity between strata.
criticisms.quote: In consideration of the heterogeneity between strata 1 and 2, the overall results pertaining to the primary eﬃcacy endpoint need careful interpretation.
